title: SQL built by concatenation (go) — review required
description: A go query call assembles SQL from parts: db.Query("SELECT " + id). If any part is untrusted input, the query structure itself is attacker-controlled. This lexical rule flags the assembly; the reviewer confirms every part is trusted or parameterizes it.
remediation: Parameterize with $1 placeholders so input stays data; never interpolate values into SQL text.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: any concatenated query matches, including trusted assembly. Input trust needs human review.

tests.line: rows, err := db.Query(fmt.Sprintf("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '%s'", name))
rows, err := db.QueryContext(ctx, "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = $1", name)
